reason: B is native iOS: bold large title, inset-grouped list, green UISwitch, value-and-chevron rows, footer text, and AX-XL rows that reflow cleanly. A looks like Material on iOS: a thin non-native title, M3-style switches, a hand-rolled segmented control and icon on every row. At AX-XL, A breaks 'notification/s' mid-word and squeezes the toggle column.

B has one dominant hero figure with smaller cents and currency symbol, plain native iOS styling (large title, standard tab bar), restrained monochrome accents with red only for over-budget, and it reflows cleanly at AX-XL. A is Material-styled (pill tab indicator, floating Add-expense button) and its button covers the hero text at AX-XL. A also stacks many tinted cards and icons.

A reads as native iOS: bold large title, inset-grouped lists, system toggles, and specific footer copy. At AX-XL its rows reflow cleanly, though the email breaks mid-word. B's title is regular weight with no clear hierarchy, adds an icon to every row, and uses a hand-rolled pill segmented control with tinted headers. At AX-XL it splits words ('notification / s') and pushes icons into the margin.

B has one dominant hero figure with a smaller $ and cents, a native bold large title, inset grouped rows and monochrome glyphs. At AX-XL its chips wrap and its rows stack cleanly. A's balance card has nested stat chips, tinted icon tiles and pink Pending pills. Its title is thin and off-platform, and its filter chips get clipped at AX-XL.

A buries the plan picker under the sticky CTA at default size, so neither price is visible. Its tinted icon tiles and gradient app icon add noise. B shows Monthly vs Yearly cards with a clear selection, per-month equivalent, Save 44% badge, trial timeline, price disclosure and Terms/Privacy. Its monochrome styling is restrained. At AX-XL, B's checkmarks don't scale and both clip content behind the CTA.

A is restrained, with one accent and a clear headline-to-CTA path. Its AX-XL footer stays compact, but the feature rows get clipped under it. B's mock-note card is domain-true and its dark mode is better tuned, but the card competes with the headline. At AX-XL, B's sticky footer takes over half the screen and the CTA icon sits out of line with its label.

A has one dominant figure with de-emphasized cents, restrained monochrome where red appears only for overspend, an iOS large title, and stats that reflow cleanly at AX-XL. B uses Material chrome (a FAB and a pill nav indicator), a weak thin title, and a mint card. Its FAB covers the budget rows and clips the per-day text at AX-XL.

A has one clear focal number with a muted $ and cents, an inset grouped list and a bold large title, and its rows reflow cleanly at AX-XL. B stacks pill cards inside a tinted card, adds colored icon tiles and pink badges, and uses a light-weight title that does not grow at AX-XL. B's filter chips clip at AX-XL. B does have richer content: daily totals and payroll.

A is restrained: neutral palette, a single black CTA, a native-style Size row and a clean type ramp. B's colour swatches render as empty circles, which is a defect, and they are near-invisible in dark mode. B also uses a lot of accent (peach, brown, badge, discount). A's weak spot is AX-XL, where the price is clipped behind the sticky CTA. B reflows its large text better.

A's colour swatches render as empty circles. Its size picker sits hidden under the sticky bar, and the price appears twice. The orange accent shows up in many places and competes with the CTA. B is restrained, with real swatches, a native-style size row and a dominant CTA. However, at AX-XL the CTA covers and clips B's price, and its dark mode is flatter.

B has a native bold large title, a single hero number, a restrained chart with one accent, and a stat row plus a real runs list. A layers pink-on-pink cards, a redundant goal ring, a thin non-bold title and pill confetti. Both strain at AX-XL: B's trend line wraps badly and its chevrons drift, while A's ring and chevrons get cramped.

A shows both plans and prices above the fold, uses a single accent, pins the CTA, includes a price disclosure and adapts its dark-mode CTA. B uses a template (centered icon plus tinted feature-icon confetti) and pushes the plans below the CTA, so no prices are visible. Its light-mode status bar is invisible, and at AX-XL the X button doesn't scale.

A's live note preview is the most domain-true element here, but it pulls focus from the headline. Purple appears on nearly every element. A half-visible row peeks above the CTA bar. At AX-XL, A's card fails: the play button floats beside wrapped text and the CTA icon stays tiny. B is restrained, with one orange accent and a dominant headline, and it scrolls cleanly at AX-XL. B's dark mode is flatter.

A has one clear hero number, uses a single accent once (Thu bar), a native large title and an inset-grouped list, and its tabular stats add up (7.0+8.4+6.2=21.6). B is cards on a tinted background, with chips and a goal ring that compete with the hero. Its 'This Week' title is regular weight and reads Oct 6–12 on Oct 15. At AX-XL, B's ring doesn't scale with the text. A's date row wraps awkwardly but holds.

A has a confident editorial headline, product-specific copy and a restrained button stack that ranks Apple first, then Google, then email. Its weak spots are the large empty gap in the middle and a stray divider line. B has two competing primary buttons (black Apple and purple email), purple accent on links too, icon-heavy fields and generic 'Welcome back' copy. At the largest text size, both scroll and push the Apple glyph away from its label.

B has a confident left-aligned hero, a single focal Apple CTA, and quiet tinted secondaries in a thumb-zone bottom bar, plus legal copy and specific domain copy. A's black Apple button and purple email CTA compete, and the inline web-style form adds clutter. At AX-XL, A clips the Google button. B keeps the CTA pinned, but its other options are hidden. Both leave the Apple glyph small.
